questions.question: Write a sequence of manufacture for the rescue device model and explain why the order matters, with one example.
questions.expected_answer: Mark out all parts from the working drawing; cut the base, arms, pivot block and saddles; laminate the arms and base and dry under weight; punch pivot and rod holes; glue the block and saddles to the base; fit the arms to the block with a split pin; make the rod and pin it to the arms and plunger; fill the syringes and tube under water and connect; mount the syringe in its saddles; test, adjust and finish. Order matters because some steps make later ones impossible or weak: for example, if the pivot block is glued down before its hole is punched, the hole cannot be made cleanly, and if the arms are assembled before the glue has dried they will delaminate.

questions.question: Describe three safety rules for making the model and explain how to make the arms stiff and the joints free of slack.
questions.expected_answer: Use a craft knife only on a cutting mat against a steel ruler, cutting away from the body with the free hand behind the blade, in light passes, capping it when put down; carry scissors closed and never point a syringe at anyone; clear offcuts and use glue in a ventilated space. Arms are made stiff by gluing two strips face to face with the corrugations crossed and pressing them flat. Joints are kept free of slack by punching rather than cutting holes so pins turn freely without wobble, and by fastening the rod firmly to the plunger with a tight loop and to the arms with split pins so that every millimetre of plunger movement reaches the arms.

questions.question: Explain how you would test the finished model against its specifications, and what a good evaluation and communication of the project should contain.
questions.expected_answer: Test each specification with a measurement: measure the jaw opening, load a 50 gram block and check it is held without slipping, operate from 30 centimetres away, check the model stands unaided, that arms do not bend visibly and that it works ten times; record met, partly met or not met with the figure, fix faults such as a slipping jaw or flexing arm and record each fix. The evaluation judges whether the brief was met, explains any missed specifications and proposes improvements, and reviews the process, sequence, time and safety. Communication presents the complete design record, brief, investigations, sketches, drawings, parts list, sequence, test results and evaluation, with a short explanation to the class of how the model demonstrates the principle of the real tool.
